aws_guard_duty_trusted_entity_set: `aws_guard_duty_trusted_entity_set` is GuardDuty's newer, broader trusted list, covering domains as well as IP addresses, that an `aws_guard_duty_detector` never generates findings against, GuardDuty's recommended replacement for the IP-only `aws_guard_duty_ipset`. Introduced September 2025.
aws_health_imaging_datastore: `aws_health_imaging_datastore` is the real, central repository AWS HealthImaging stores medical imaging data in, DICOM P10 files imported from S3 and transformed into image sets of metadata and pixel-data image frames, built for petabyte-scale, subsecond image retrieval.
aws_health_lake_data_transformation_prof: `aws_health_lake_data_transformation_profile` defines the real, AI-assisted mapping rules HealthLake's Data Transformation Agent uses to convert legacy healthcare data, C-CDA documents or relational data, into FHIR R4 resources, created as a mutable draft and promoted to an immutable, published version once ready. Announced in preview in March 2026, genuinely new enough that this session verified it live rather than trusting a remembered description.
aws_health_lake_fhirdatastore: `aws_health_lake_fhirdatastore` creates a real, managed, FHIR R4-compliant datastore that AWS HealthLake stores and indexes structured health data in, queryable directly through the FHIR API rather than a caller building their own FHIR server.
aws_iam_access_key: `aws_iam_access_key` issues a real, long-lived programmatic credential, an access key ID and secret, for an `aws_iam_user`, the actual credential used for CLI and SDK calls made as that user rather than through a browser session.
aws_iam_group: `aws_iam_group` creates a real, named collection of IAM users, letting a caller attach a policy once to the group and have it apply to every current and future user added to it, rather than attaching the same policy to each user individually.
aws_iam_group_policy: `aws_iam_group_policy` attaches a real inline IAM policy directly to an `aws_iam_group`, embedded in the group itself rather than existing as a separate, reusable `aws_iam_policy` that could also be attached elsewhere.
aws_iam_instance_profile: `aws_iam_instance_profile` wraps an `aws_iam_role` in the real container EC2 actually requires to attach that role's permissions to a running instance, an instance can't assume a role directly without one.
aws_iam_managed_policy: `aws_iam_managed_policy` creates a real, standalone, reusable IAM policy document that can be attached to many users, groups, and roles at once, and updated in one place to change permissions everywhere it's attached, AWS's own recommended alternative to an inline policy embedded directly in a single identity.
aws_iam_oidcprovider: `aws_iam_oidcprovider` establishes real trust between IAM and an external OpenID Connect identity provider, GitHub Actions or an EKS cluster's own OIDC issuer among common ones, so an `aws_iam_role` can be assumed directly using that provider's tokens instead of a long-lived IAM credential.
aws_iam_policy: `aws_iam_policy` creates a standalone, reusable IAM policy, a real JSON document describing what's allowed. It grants nothing on its own, attach it to a role or user with `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` to actually apply it.
aws_iam_role: An IAM role grants a set of permissions to whatever's allowed to assume it, an EC2 instance, a Lambda function, another AWS account. `aws_iam_role` creates the role and its trust policy, real permissions are attached separately, via `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment`.
aws_iam_role_policy: `aws_iam_role_policy` attaches a real inline IAM policy directly to an `aws_iam_role`, embedded in the role itself rather than existing as a separate, reusable `aws_iam_policy` that could also be attached elsewhere.
aws_iam_role_policy_attachment: `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` is the actual grant, it attaches an existing, standalone policy to an existing role. Neither the role nor the policy alone grants anything, this attachment is what connects them.
aws_iam_samlprovider: `aws_iam_samlprovider` establishes real trust between IAM and an external SAML 2.0 identity provider, a corporate Active Directory Federation Services setup, for instance, so a workforce user can federate into an `aws_iam_role` using their existing enterprise credentials rather than a separate IAM identity.
aws_iam_server_certificate: `aws_iam_server_certificate` uploads a real X.509 certificate and private key to IAM for use with a Classic Load Balancer or CloudFront, IAM's original, legacy certificate storage from before AWS Certificate Manager existed to handle this instead.
aws_iam_service_linked_role: `aws_iam_service_linked_role` creates a real IAM role predefined by an AWS service, with a trust policy and permissions the service itself owns and controls, that account owners cannot edit and generally cannot delete while the service still has resources depending on it.
aws_iam_user: `aws_iam_user` creates a real, individual IAM identity, distinct from an `aws_iam_role`, meant for a long-lived person or application that needs its own durable credentials rather than assuming temporary ones.
aws_iam_user_policy: `aws_iam_user_policy` attaches a real inline IAM policy directly to an `aws_iam_user`, embedded in the user itself rather than existing as a separate, reusable `aws_iam_policy` that could also be attached elsewhere.
aws_iam_user_to_group_addition: `aws_iam_user_to_group_addition` is the real, actual membership grant adding an `aws_iam_user` to an `aws_iam_group`. Neither existing alone makes a user a group member, this addition is what connects them.
aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice: `aws_iam_virtual_mfadevice` registers a real, software-based MFA device, an authenticator app rather than a physical hardware token, that gets assigned to an `aws_iam_user` or the account root user to require a second factor at sign-in.
aws_identity_store_group: `aws_identity_store_group` creates a real group in the Identity Store, the built-in directory behind IAM Identity Center, that `aws_sso_permission_set` assignments and application access can be granted to collectively rather than user by user.
aws_identity_store_group_membership: `aws_identity_store_group_membership` adds a real user as a member of an `aws_identity_store_group`, the resource that actually grants that user whatever access has been assigned to the group.
aws_image_builder_component: `aws_image_builder_component` defines a real, reusable build or test step, install a package, run a script, validate a setting, in YAML or JSON, that an EC2 Image Builder image pipeline assembles together to produce a custom AMI or container image.
aws_image_builder_container_recipe: `aws_image_builder_container_recipe` defines the real base container image and the ordered build and test components applied to it, that an `aws_image_builder_image_pipeline` runs to actually produce a new container image, the container-image counterpart to `aws_image_builder_image_recipe`.
aws_image_builder_distribution_configura: `aws_image_builder_distribution_configuration` defines which real Regions and accounts an `aws_image_builder_image_pipeline`'s output gets copied and shared to once built, rather than a caller manually copying a new AMI everywhere it's needed.
aws_image_builder_image: `aws_image_builder_image` is the real, actual output, an AMI or container image, produced by running an `aws_image_builder_image_pipeline` once, either on its own recurring schedule or triggered manually.
aws_image_builder_image_pipeline: `aws_image_builder_image_pipeline` automates the recurring build, test, and distribution of a real machine image or container image, combining an `aws_image_builder_image_recipe` or `aws_image_builder_container_recipe` with build infrastructure and an `aws_image_builder_distribution_configuration` into one scheduled, repeatable process.
aws_image_builder_image_recipe: `aws_image_builder_image_recipe` defines the real base AMI and the ordered build and test components applied to it, that an `aws_image_builder_image_pipeline` runs to actually produce a new, hardened, updated AMI.
aws_image_builder_infrastructure_configu: `aws_image_builder_infrastructure_configuration` defines the real EC2 environment, instance type, subnet, IAM instance profile, that Image Builder launches temporary build instances into while assembling an image from `aws_image_builder_component`s.
aws_image_builder_lifecycle_policy: `aws_image_builder_lifecycle_policy` automatically deprecates or deletes an `aws_image_builder_image_pipeline`'s older real output images on a defined schedule, real cleanup that keeps old, unpatched AMIs from accumulating indefinitely.
aws_image_builder_workflow: `aws_image_builder_workflow` defines a real, custom sequence of build, test, and distribution steps for EC2 Image Builder, an alternative to its own default workflow when a pipeline needs steps in a different order or with custom logic between them.
aws_inspector_assessment_target: `aws_inspector_assessment_target` defined a real, tag-based group of EC2 instances that an `aws_inspector_assessment_template` ran a security assessment against, in Amazon Inspector Classic, the original architecture Amazon Inspector shipped with. Inspector Classic is no longer available to new accounts, or to accounts that haven't run an assessment in the last 6 months, and reaches full end of support on May 20, 2026; the redesigned Amazon Inspector (Inspector v2) is the current, actively developed service.
aws_inspector_assessment_template: `aws_inspector_assessment_template` defined the real rules packages and duration for a security assessment run against an `aws_inspector_assessment_target` in Amazon Inspector Classic. Reaches full end of support May 20, 2026, alongside the rest of Inspector Classic.
aws_inspector_resource_group: `aws_inspector_resource_group` was the real, tag-based filter defining exactly which EC2 instances belonged to an `aws_inspector_assessment_target` in Amazon Inspector Classic. Reaches full end of support May 20, 2026, alongside the rest of Inspector Classic.
aws_inspector_v2_cis_scan_configuration: `aws_inspector_v2_cis_scan_configuration` schedules real, recurring CIS benchmark compliance scans against EC2 instances, checking actual operating-system configuration against a defined CIS standard rather than the vulnerability scanning Inspector v2 otherwise focuses on.
aws_inspector_v2_code_security_integrati: `aws_inspector_v2_code_security_integration` connects Amazon Inspector to a real source-code platform, GitHub or GitLab, so Inspector's Code Security capability can scan up to 100,000 real repositories' default branches for vulnerabilities directly in the source, shifting detection left of a deployed, running resource. Launched June 2025.
aws_inspector_v2_code_security_scan_conf: `aws_inspector_v2_code_security_scan_configuration` defines real scanning rules, applied by default to every new repository or scoped to specific ones by tag, under an `aws_inspector_v2_code_security_integration`, up to three default configurations per project.
aws_inspector_v2_connector: `aws_inspector_v2_connector` is the real, account-level connection Amazon Inspector's Code Security capability uses to reach a specific source-code provider account, the resource an `aws_inspector_v2_code_security_integration` is actually built on top of.
aws_inspector_v2_filter: `aws_inspector_v2_filter` suppresses, or routes to a specific notification, real Inspector v2 findings matching defined criteria, severity, resource type, package name, cutting down alert noise from findings a caller has already triaged or determined aren't actionable.
aws_instance: `aws_instance` launches a real, virtual server, an EC2 instance, in the AWS Cloud, its instance type determining the actual balance of compute, memory, network, and storage hardware available to it. It's the single most fundamental EC2 resource, the one an AMI, a key pair, a security group, and an EBS volume all ultimately attach to or run on.
aws_interconnect_connection: `aws_interconnect_connection` (AWS::DirectConnect::Interconnect) is a real, physical connection, over standard Ethernet fiber, between an AWS Direct Connect Partner's own network and a Direct Connect location, that the partner uses to provision and resell hosted Direct Connect connections to their own customers, rather than each customer needing a direct physical link to AWS themselves.
aws_internet_gateway: `aws_internet_gateway` is a real, horizontally scaled, redundant VPC component that allows communication between resources in a VPC and the internet, the actual resource an `aws_route` with a 0.0.0.0/0 destination points traffic at for a subnet to be genuinely public.
aws_internet_monitor_monitor: `aws_internet_monitor_monitor` uses AWS's own global networking data, cross-referenced against a defined set of resources, VPCs, CloudFront distributions, WorkSpaces, to continuously measure real internet performance and availability between an application and its actual end users, and alert on regional disruptions or unusual latency without a caller needing external synthetic monitoring.
aws_invoicing_invoice_unit: `aws_invoicing_invoice_unit` groups a real, mutually exclusive set of member accounts into one business entity, a subsidiary, a legal entity, a cost center, so AWS issues that entity its own separate invoice rather than one combined invoice for an entire AWS Organization. Reached general availability December 2024.
aws_io_t_account_audit_configuration: `aws_io_t_account_audit_configuration` turns on AWS IoT Device Defender's real, account-wide audit checks, security-related misconfigurations across an account's things, certificates, and policies, that an `aws_io_t_scheduled_audit` then runs on a recurring basis.
aws_io_t_authorizer: `aws_io_t_authorizer` runs a real, caller-defined Lambda function to authenticate and authorize a device's connection using a custom token scheme, rather than the X.509 certificate model `aws_io_t_certificate` and `aws_io_t_policy` provide.
aws_io_t_billing_group: `aws_io_t_billing_group` organizes real `aws_io_t_thing`s for cost allocation and tracking purposes, kept separate from an `aws_io_t_thing_group`'s own operational grouping.
aws_io_t_cacertificate: `aws_io_t_cacertificate` registers a real, caller-owned certificate authority with AWS IoT, so device certificates the caller's own CA issues, rather than only ones AWS IoT itself issues, can be trusted to authenticate an `aws_io_t_thing`'s connection.
aws_io_t_certificate: `aws_io_t_certificate` is a real X.509 certificate AWS IoT issues or registers for device authentication, the actual credential an `aws_io_t_thing` presents to authenticate its MQTT or HTTPS connection to AWS IoT Core.
aws_io_t_certificate_provider: `aws_io_t_certificate_provider` runs a real, caller-defined Lambda function during Fleet Provisioning to issue a device's `aws_io_t_certificate` dynamically, using a custom or third-party CA, rather than relying only on AWS IoT's own certificate issuance.
aws_io_t_command: `aws_io_t_command` defines a real, reusable, named remote command with its own custom payload schema, that AWS IoT Device Management Commands sends to a targeted device and tracks execution status for, without a caller managing MQTT topics, payload formats, or status tracking by hand. Reached general availability November 2024.
aws_io_t_custom_metric: `aws_io_t_custom_metric` defines a real, caller-specific metric, beyond AWS IoT's own built-in ones, that a device reports and an `aws_io_t_security_profile` can evaluate as part of Device Defender's behavioral detection.
aws_io_t_dimension: `aws_io_t_dimension` scopes an `aws_io_t_security_profile`'s own behavior checks to a real, defined subset, a specific set of MQTT topics, for instance, rather than the profile applying uniformly across everything a device does.
aws_io_t_domain_configuration: `aws_io_t_domain_configuration` lets devices connect to AWS IoT Core over a real, custom domain name and TLS configuration instead of the default AWS-provided IoT endpoint.
aws_io_t_encryption_configuration: `aws_io_t_encryption_configuration` sets a real, caller-managed KMS key that AWS IoT Core uses to encrypt data at rest account-wide, in place of AWS's own default encryption key.
aws_io_t_fleet_metric: `aws_io_t_fleet_metric` aggregates a real CloudWatch metric across every device in an `aws_io_t_thing_group`, fleet-wide visibility, average battery level across a whole product line, for instance, rather than only per-device metrics.
aws_io_t_job: `aws_io_t_job` defines a real, remote operation, a firmware update, a config change, a reboot command, deployed to and tracked across one or more real `aws_io_t_thing`s or `aws_io_t_thing_group`s, with per-device execution status reported back to AWS IoT.
aws_io_t_job_template: `aws_io_t_job_template` is a real, reusable configuration, rollout rate, timeout, abort criteria, that an `aws_io_t_job` can be created from, so the same recurring job shape doesn't need to be configured from scratch every time.
aws_io_t_logging: `aws_io_t_logging` configures real, account-wide CloudWatch Logs delivery for AWS IoT Core activity, connection attempts, rule executions, errors, at a defined verbosity level.
aws_io_t_mitigation_action: `aws_io_t_mitigation_action` defines a real, automated remediation, revoking a certificate, adding a device to a quarantine thing group, that an `aws_io_t_scheduled_audit`'s findings can trigger automatically rather than requiring a human to act on every audit finding.
aws_io_t_policy: `aws_io_t_policy` is a real, JSON-based document defining exactly which MQTT topics and AWS IoT actions a connected device is actually allowed to publish, subscribe to, or invoke, attached to an `aws_io_t_certificate` through an `aws_io_t_policy_principal_attachment`.
aws_io_t_policy_principal_attachment: `aws_io_t_policy_principal_attachment` is the real, actual grant attaching an `aws_io_t_policy` to a specific certificate or other principal. A policy with nothing attached to it authorizes no real device's connection.
aws_io_t_provisioning_template: `aws_io_t_provisioning_template` defines the real resources, an `aws_io_t_thing`, a certificate, policy attachments, that AWS IoT Fleet Provisioning automatically creates the first time a new device connects, so a device can be manufactured with generic bootstrap credentials rather than a unique certificate burned in at the factory.
aws_io_t_resource_specific_logging: `aws_io_t_resource_specific_logging` configures real, per-resource IoT Core logging levels, overriding the account's own default logging level for a specific thing, thing group, or topic when only that resource's traffic needs closer visibility.
aws_io_t_role_alias: `aws_io_t_role_alias` lets a real, authenticated device exchange its `aws_io_t_certificate` for temporary AWS credentials tied to a specific IAM role, through the IoT credentials provider, without embedding a long-lived AWS access key on the device itself.
aws_io_t_scheduled_audit: `aws_io_t_scheduled_audit` runs Device Defender's real, configured audit checks on a recurring schedule, defined by an `aws_io_t_account_audit_configuration`, real, ongoing compliance checking rather than a one-time manual review.
aws_io_t_security_profile: `aws_io_t_security_profile` defines real, expected behavior for a group of devices, connection frequency, message size, authorization failures, that Device Defender's Detect capability continuously measures live device behavior against, alerting when a device deviates from its own defined profile.
aws_io_t_software_package: `aws_io_t_software_package` is a real, named entry in the AWS IoT Software Package Catalog, an inventory of firmware, OS updates, or applications, whose `aws_io_t_software_package_version`s get associated with things and deployed through an `aws_io_t_job`. Reached general availability in 2023.
aws_io_t_software_package_version: `aws_io_t_software_package_version` is one real, specific, deployable version, a set of actual files, firmware, configuration, security patches, of an `aws_io_t_software_package`.
aws_io_t_stream: `aws_io_t_stream` delivers a real, large file, a firmware image, in ordered chunks over MQTT to a device running an `aws_io_t_job`, AWS IoT's own mechanism for file delivery to devices that can't make a normal HTTPS download request.
aws_io_t_thing: `aws_io_t_thing` registers a real device or logical entity in the AWS IoT registry, the actual identity an `aws_io_t_certificate` gets attached to and an `aws_io_t_policy` ultimately governs the permissions of.
aws_io_t_thing_group: `aws_io_t_thing_group` is a real, static or dynamic (query-based) collection of `aws_io_t_thing`s, the actual grouping an `aws_io_t_job` or `aws_io_t_fleet_metric` targets rather than every operation addressing individual things one at a time.
aws_io_t_thing_principal_attachment: `aws_io_t_thing_principal_attachment` is the real, actual link between an `aws_io_t_thing` and its `aws_io_t_certificate`. A certificate with no thing attachment can still authenticate an MQTT connection but has no thing identity behind it.
aws_io_t_thing_type: `aws_io_t_thing_type` defines a real, reusable template of common attributes and searchable metadata for a category of `aws_io_t_thing`s, temperature sensors versus door locks, for instance, rather than every thing's attributes being defined from scratch.
aws_io_t_topic_rule: `aws_io_t_topic_rule` is a real, SQL-like rule the AWS IoT Rules Engine evaluates against every message published to a matching MQTT topic, routing matching messages to a real target, Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, an `aws_io_tanalytics_channel`, and dozens of other AWS services.
aws_io_t_topic_rule_destination: `aws_io_t_topic_rule_destination` registers a real HTTPS endpoint an `aws_io_t_topic_rule` can send matched messages to, requiring the endpoint to confirm ownership before AWS IoT will actually deliver any traffic to it.
aws_io_tanalytics_channel: `aws_io_tanalytics_channel` is the real entry point AWS IoT Analytics ingests raw device messages into, typically fed directly by an `aws_io_t_topic_rule`, and holds the unprocessed data an `aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline` reads from.
aws_io_tanalytics_dataset: `aws_io_tanalytics_dataset` runs a real, recurring SQL query or containerized analysis against an `aws_io_tanalytics_datastore` and materializes the result, the actual output a caller or downstream application reads insights from.
aws_io_tanalytics_datastore: `aws_io_tanalytics_datastore` holds the real, processed output of an `aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline`, the actual data an `aws_io_tanalytics_dataset`'s query or container runs against.
aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline: `aws_io_tanalytics_pipeline` is a real, ordered sequence of activities, filtering, enriching, transforming, that processes messages from an `aws_io_tanalytics_channel` and writes the result into an `aws_io_tanalytics_datastore`.
aws_io_tcore_device_advisor_suite_defini: `aws_io_tcore_device_advisor_suite_definition` defines a real, pre-built or custom test suite that validates a device's software against AWS IoT Core's own best practices, connection reliability, MQTT compliance, before that device ships to production, catching real integration issues in a controlled test environment rather than in the field.
aws_io_tevents_alarm_model: `aws_io_tevents_alarm_model` is a real, pre-built alarm pattern, built on the same underlying state-machine mechanism as an `aws_io_tevents_detector_model`, purpose-built for the common case of a threshold-based alarm rather than a caller designing a full custom state machine for it.
aws_io_tevents_detector_model: `aws_io_tevents_detector_model` is a real state machine, defined states and the events that transition between them, that AWS IoT Events runs one instance of per real, tracked entity, an individual piece of equipment, a process, evaluating incoming data against it continuously to detect real operational states like a stuck valve or an overheating motor.
aws_io_tevents_input: `aws_io_tevents_input` defines the real message attributes an `aws_io_tevents_detector_model` actually evaluates, the structured data a detector model's states and transitions are written in terms of.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign` defines real, specific data collection rules, which signals, at what rate, under what trigger condition, deployed to an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle` or `aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet`'s own Edge Agent. Part of AWS IoT FleetWise, which is no longer open to new customers.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_decoder_manifest` translates a real vehicle's raw CAN bus or OBD messages into the named signals an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest` defines, the actual decoding logic the Edge Agent applies on the vehicle itself. Part of AWS IoT FleetWise, which is no longer open to new customers.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_fleet` is a real, logical grouping of `aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle`s that an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign` can target together rather than every vehicle being addressed individually. Part of AWS IoT FleetWise, which is no longer open to new customers.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest` selects the real, specific signals from an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog` that apply to one vehicle model, the actual signal set an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle` of that model can report. Part of AWS IoT FleetWise, which is no longer open to new customers.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_signal_catalog` is a real, comprehensive catalog of every vehicle signal, engine RPM, door status, that an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_model_manifest` selects a relevant subset from for one specific vehicle model. Part of AWS IoT FleetWise, which is no longer open to new customers.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template` tracks a real, defined set of signals' current state on a vehicle, reported on change or on a periodic interval by the Edge Agent, distinct from an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign`'s own bulk data-collection model. Part of AWS IoT FleetWise, which is no longer open to new customers.
aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle: `aws_io_tfleet_wise_vehicle` registers a real, individual vehicle running the AWS IoT FleetWise Edge Agent, the actual entity an `aws_io_tfleet_wise_campaign` and `aws_io_tfleet_wise_state_template` get associated with to collect data from. AWS IoT FleetWise is no longer open to new customers; existing customers can continue using it, with AWS pointing to its Guidance for Connected Mobility on AWS for equivalent new capability.
aws_io_tsecure_tunneling_tunnel: `aws_io_tsecure_tunneling_tunnel` is an AWS IoT Secure Tunneling tunnel, a real, temporary bidirectional communication channel to a remote device (e.g. one behind a firewall or NAT with no open inbound ports) for troubleshooting or remote access, brokered entirely by AWS IoT rather than requiring inbound connectivity to the device itself.
aws_io_tsite_wise_access_policy: `aws_io_tsite_wise_access_policy` grants a real IAM user, group, or IAM Identity Center identity permission to view or administer a specific `aws_io_tsite_wise_portal`, SiteWise Monitor's own access-control mechanism separate from IAM policies on the underlying SiteWise API.
aws_io_tsite_wise_asset: `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset` represents one real, physical piece of industrial equipment, created from an `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model`, that an `aws_io_tsite_wise_gateway` streams real, live sensor data into.
aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model: `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model` is a real, reusable template defining the properties, hierarchy, and computed metrics common to a category of equipment, a wind turbine model, for instance, that every `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset` created from it automatically inherits.
aws_io_tsite_wise_computation_model: `aws_io_tsite_wise_computation_model` defines a real, reusable computation, a transform, metric, or anomaly-detection model, that binds to asset or asset-model properties through a named data-binding configuration, so the same calculation logic can be shared and applied consistently across `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset_model`s rather than redefined inside each one individually. Verified live against AWS's own CloudFormation reference this session, resolving last session's flagged, unverified version of this entry.
aws_io_tsite_wise_dashboard: `aws_io_tsite_wise_dashboard` is a real, saved visualization, trend charts, KPIs, of `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset` data inside an `aws_io_tsite_wise_project`.
aws_io_tsite_wise_dataset: `aws_io_tsite_wise_dataset` links a real, external structured dataset, maintenance records, work orders, to `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset` data, so operational context beyond raw sensor readings can be queried and visualized alongside it.
aws_io_tsite_wise_gateway: `aws_io_tsite_wise_gateway` is real, on-premises software that collects data from industrial protocols, OPC-UA among them, and streams it into an `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset`'s properties, the actual bridge between a factory floor and SiteWise's own cloud-based asset model.
aws_io_tsite_wise_portal: `aws_io_tsite_wise_portal` is a real, managed web application, with its own users and access control, through which SiteWise data actually gets visualized, the container an `aws_io_tsite_wise_project` and its dashboards live inside.
aws_io_tsite_wise_project: `aws_io_tsite_wise_project` groups a real set of `aws_io_tsite_wise_asset`s and `aws_io_tsite_wise_dashboard`s inside an `aws_io_tsite_wise_portal`, organizing what a specific team or use case actually sees when they open the portal.
aws_io_tthings_graph_flow_template: `aws_io_tthings_graph_flow_template` defined a real, visual workflow connecting multiple devices and services together in AWS IoT Things Graph. AWS IoT Things Graph was fully discontinued and transitioned to AWS IoT TwinMaker on November 9, 2022; its APIs are deprecated, kept only for backward compatibility, and should not be used for new work.
aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type: `aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type` is a real, reusable definition of properties and behavior, a temperature sensor's own data schema, for instance, that an `aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity` in an `aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace` can be built from.
aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity: `aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity` is the real, digital representation of one physical object, a specific machine, a room, built from one or more `aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type`s inside an `aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace`.
aws_io_ttwin_maker_scene: `aws_io_ttwin_maker_scene` composes a real, 3D visualization of an `aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace`'s own entities, tagging real-time data onto a 3D model rather than only viewing entity data as raw numbers.
aws_io_ttwin_maker_sync_job: `aws_io_ttwin_maker_sync_job` keeps an `aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace`'s own entities automatically synchronized with a real, external source of truth, so a digital twin doesn't drift out of date with the physical or logical system it represents.
aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace: `aws_io_ttwin_maker_workspace` is the real, top-level AWS IoT TwinMaker container an `aws_io_ttwin_maker_entity`, `aws_io_ttwin_maker_component_type`, and `aws_io_ttwin_maker_scene` all belong to, the digital twin project every other TwinMaker resource is scoped inside.
aws_io_twireless_destination: `aws_io_twireless_destination` routes a real, decoded LoRaWAN or Sidewalk message from an `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device` to an `aws_io_t_topic_rule`, the actual bridge from AWS IoT Wireless into the rest of AWS IoT Core.
aws_io_twireless_device_profile: `aws_io_twireless_device_profile` is a real, reusable template of LoRaWAN device capabilities, supported data rates, class type, applied to an `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device` rather than every device's radio characteristics being configured individually.
aws_io_twireless_fuota_task: `aws_io_twireless_fuota_task` runs a real firmware-update-over-the-air campaign across a group of LoRaWAN `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device`s, using multicast delivery to update many devices' firmware efficiently rather than one at a time.
aws_io_twireless_multicast_group: `aws_io_twireless_multicast_group` sends the real, same LoRaWAN downlink message to a defined group of `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device`s at once, rather than a caller addressing every device in the group individually.
aws_io_twireless_network_analyzer_config: `aws_io_twireless_network_analyzer_configuration` defines a real, live traffic-tracing session scoped to specific `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device`s or gateways, for debugging LoRaWAN connectivity issues as they actually happen rather than after the fact from logs alone.
aws_io_twireless_partner_account: `aws_io_twireless_partner_account` links a real Amazon Sidewalk partner account to AWS IoT Wireless, required before a caller's own Sidewalk `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device`s can be managed through the service.
aws_io_twireless_service_profile: `aws_io_twireless_service_profile` is a real, reusable template of LoRaWAN network server behavior, applied to an `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device` alongside its own `aws_io_twireless_device_profile`.
aws_io_twireless_task_definition: `aws_io_twireless_task_definition` is the real, reusable firmware update definition, the actual image and update parameters, that an `aws_io_twireless_fuota_task` deploys.
aws_io_twireless_wireless_device: `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device` registers a real, individual LoRaWAN or Amazon Sidewalk device with AWS IoT Wireless, the actual endpoint that connects through an `aws_io_twireless_wireless_gateway` to AWS IoT Core.
aws_io_twireless_wireless_device_import_: `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device_import_task` bulk-imports real Sidewalk devices from a manufacturer-provided list into AWS IoT Wireless as `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device`s, rather than a caller registering each device one at a time.
aws_io_twireless_wireless_gateway: `aws_io_twireless_wireless_gateway` registers a real LoRaWAN gateway, the physical radio hardware that receives transmissions from an `aws_io_twireless_wireless_device` and forwards them to AWS IoT Wireless.
aws_ivs_channel: `aws_ivs_channel` is the real, core Amazon IVS resource a broadcaster streams video into and viewers watch from, with its own ingest endpoint, playback URL, and configurable latency mode.
aws_ivs_encoder_configuration: `aws_ivs_encoder_configuration` sets real encoding parameters, resolution, bitrate, for Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming, applied to participants in an `aws_ivs_stage` rather than a single broadcast `aws_ivs_channel`.
aws_ivs_ingest_configuration: `aws_ivs_ingest_configuration` specifies a real, named ingest protocol, RTMP or RTMPS, for broadcasting into a specific `aws_ivs_stage`'s real-time stage, including whether insecure RTMP ingest is allowed and an optional customer-assigned user ID used to link the ingest participant to the customer's own systems. Verified live against AWS's own CloudFormation reference this session, resolving last session's flagged, unverified version of this entry.
aws_ivs_playback_key_pair: `aws_ivs_playback_key_pair` signs real, private playback tokens for an `aws_ivs_channel` configured to require authorization, restricting viewing to clients that present a token signed by this specific key pair.
aws_ivs_playback_restriction_policy: `aws_ivs_playback_restriction_policy` restricts real playback of an `aws_ivs_channel` by geography or origin domain, blocking viewers outside an allowed country list or a site that isn't the caller's own from embedding the stream.
aws_ivs_public_key: `aws_ivs_public_key` registers a real public key IVS validates participant tokens for an `aws_ivs_stage` against, the Real-Time Streaming counterpart to `aws_ivs_playback_key_pair`'s own channel-playback authorization.
aws_ivs_recording_configuration: `aws_ivs_recording_configuration` automatically records an `aws_ivs_channel`'s live stream to a real S3 bucket as it broadcasts, so a stream is available for on-demand playback after it ends without a caller building their own recording pipeline.
aws_ivs_stage: `aws_ivs_stage` is Amazon IVS's real, low-latency, multi-participant video collaboration resource, up to several hosts and guests interacting live together, distinct from an `aws_ivs_channel`'s own single-broadcaster-to-many-viewers model.
aws_ivs_storage_configuration: `aws_ivs_storage_configuration` defines a real S3 destination that an `aws_ivs_stage`'s own composite recording gets written to, the stage counterpart to `aws_ivs_recording_configuration`'s channel-level recording.
aws_ivs_stream_key: `aws_ivs_stream_key` is the real, secret credential streaming software uses to authenticate and publish video to a specific `aws_ivs_channel`, distinct from the channel's own public ingest endpoint URL.
aws_ivschat_logging_configuration: `aws_ivschat_logging_configuration` streams a real `aws_ivschat_room`'s chat messages to a destination, CloudWatch Logs, Kinesis Data Firehose, or S3, for moderation review or analytics rather than messages existing only transiently in the room.
aws_ivschat_room: `aws_ivschat_room` creates a real, managed chat room, typically paired alongside an `aws_ivs_channel`'s live stream, that Amazon IVS Chat handles message fan-out, moderation, and connection scaling for.
aws_kafka_connect_connector: `aws_kafka_connect_connector` runs a real, managed Kafka Connect connector, MSK Connect provisioning and scaling the underlying compute, moving data between an Apache Kafka or Amazon MSK cluster and an external system without a caller operating their own Kafka Connect worker cluster.
aws_kafka_connect_custom_plugin: `aws_kafka_connect_custom_plugin` uploads the real connector code, a JDBC sink, an S3 source, that an `aws_kafka_connect_connector` actually runs, MSK Connect's own way of using a connector implementation that isn't AWS-provided.
aws_kafka_connect_worker_configuration: `aws_kafka_connect_worker_configuration` sets real Kafka Connect worker-level properties applied to an `aws_kafka_connect_connector`'s own underlying runtime, beyond the connector's specific configuration alone.
aws_kendra_data_source: `aws_kendra_data_source` connects a real content repository, S3, SharePoint, Confluence, a website, to an `aws_kendra_index`, so Kendra can crawl and index its content rather than a caller uploading documents by hand.
aws_kendra_faq: `aws_kendra_faq` loads a real, structured set of question-and-answer pairs directly into an `aws_kendra_index`, so an exact FAQ match can be surfaced with high confidence rather than relying only on Kendra's own document-search relevance.
aws_kendra_index: `aws_kendra_index` is the real, core Amazon Kendra search index, built from one or more `aws_kendra_data_source`s, that a caller's own natural-language search queries actually run against.
aws_kendra_query_suggestions_block_list: `aws_kendra_query_suggestions_block_list` blocks specific real terms from appearing in an `aws_kendra_index`'s own autocomplete query suggestions, without removing the underlying documents that contain them from search results entirely.
aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan: `aws_kendra_ranking_execution_plan` provisions Kendra Intelligent Ranking, a real, standalone semantic re-ranking API a caller applies to results from their own separate search system, OpenSearch or Elasticsearch, for instance, independent of using a full `aws_kendra_index`.
aws_kendra_thesaurus: `aws_kendra_thesaurus` teaches an `aws_kendra_index` real synonym relationships, so a search for one term also matches documents using an equivalent term, improving recall beyond exact keyword matching.
aws_key_pair: `aws_key_pair` creates or imports a real SSH key pair, AWS storing the public key and the caller keeping the private key, used to securely retrieve an `aws_instance`'s initial administrator password or authenticate an SSH connection to it.
aws_kinesis_analytics_application: `aws_kinesis_analytics_application` runs a real, continuous SQL query directly against a streaming data source, Kinesis Data Streams or Firehose, the original, SQL-based Kinesis Data Analytics application type, distinct from the newer Apache Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics v2 applications.
aws_kinesis_analytics_application_output: `aws_kinesis_analytics_application_output` defines a real destination, another Kinesis stream, a Lambda function, that an `aws_kinesis_analytics_application`'s own continuous SQL query results actually get delivered to.
aws_kinesis_analytics_application_refere: `aws_kinesis_analytics_application_reference_data_source` adds a real static reference table, loaded from an S3 object, that an `aws_kinesis_analytics_application`'s SQL can join against incoming stream records. This is scoped to the original SQL-based Kinesis Data Analytics application type, which AWS has fully discontinued: no new applications could be created after October 15, 2025, and all remaining applications were deleted and support ended on January 27, 2026, a date now in the past. The distinct, current generation is `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application`, built on Apache Flink.
aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application: `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application` runs a real Apache Flink stream-processing application, or an interactive Kinesis Data Analytics Studio notebook when its mode is set to INTERACTIVE, distinct from the now-discontinued SQL-based Kinesis Data Analytics application type this v2 generation replaced.
aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application_clo: `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application_cloud_watch_logging_option` attaches a real CloudWatch log stream to an `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application`, so the Flink application's own runtime logs land somewhere durable and queryable rather than being discarded.
aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application_out: `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application_output` adds a real external destination, a Kinesis data stream, a Firehose delivery stream, or a Lambda function, that an `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application` writes its processed results to.
aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application_ref: `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application_reference_data_source` adds a real static reference table, loaded from an S3 object, that an `aws_kinesis_analytics_v2_application`'s SQL-based code can join against incoming stream records.
aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream: `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` creates a real managed pipeline that acquires, transforms, and delivers streaming data within seconds to a destination such as S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, or a third-party analytics tool. AWS renamed the underlying service from "Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose" to "Amazon Data Firehose" in February 2024; the resource name and behavior are unchanged.
aws_kinesis_resource_policy: `aws_kinesis_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_kinesis_stream`, controlling which principals, including from other accounts, can read from or write to it.
aws_kinesis_stream: `aws_kinesis_stream` creates a real, sharded data stream that ingests and retains streaming records for a configurable window, from the default 24 hours up to 365 days, for real-time, multi-consumer processing.
aws_kinesis_stream_consumer: `aws_kinesis_stream_consumer` registers a real dedicated-throughput consumer on an `aws_kinesis_stream` using enhanced fan-out, so this one consumer gets its own 2 MB/sec-per-shard read pipe instead of sharing the stream's default throughput with every other reader.
aws_kinesis_video_signaling_channel: `aws_kinesis_video_signaling_channel` creates a real WebRTC signaling channel that exchanges the SDP offers/answers and ICE candidates needed to establish a peer-to-peer media connection between WebRTC clients, distinct from `aws_kinesis_video_stream`'s own role storing and replaying the actual media.
aws_kinesis_video_stream: `aws_kinesis_video_stream` creates a real stream that captures, stores, and indexes live video and other time-encoded data for playback and downstream analysis.
aws_kms_alias: `aws_kms_alias` creates a real, friendly name for an `aws_kms_key`, so application code and IAM policies can reference the alias rather than a key's own generated ID, and keep working unchanged if the underlying key is ever rotated to a new one.
aws_kms_key: `aws_kms_key` creates a real cryptographic key in AWS Key Management Service, symmetric encryption keys, asymmetric encryption or signing keys, or symmetric HMAC keys, and can create the multi-Region primary key that an `aws_kms_replica_key` replicates from. Changing a key's spec, usage, origin, or multi-Region setting on an existing key is blocked outright, a deliberate guard against silently destroying key material.
aws_kms_replica_key: `aws_kms_replica_key` creates a real multi-Region replica of an `aws_kms_key` primary key in a different AWS Region. A replica shares its primary's key ID, key material, key spec, key usage, and rotation status, so data encrypted under the key in one Region can be decrypted under the replica in another without a cross-Region call or exposing plaintext in transit.
aws_lake_formation_data_cells_filter: `aws_lake_formation_data_cells_filter` defines a real, fine-grained filter, restricting access to specific rows or columns of a table, that Lake Formation enforces on top of its own coarser table- and database-level `aws_lake_formation_permissions` grants.
aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings: `aws_lake_formation_data_lake_settings` configures the real account-level defaults for AWS Lake Formation, including data lake administrators and whether new Data Catalog databases and tables default to Lake Formation's own permission model or fall back to legacy IAM-only access.
aws_lake_formation_permissions: `aws_lake_formation_permissions` grants a real Lake Formation permission to a principal on a Data Catalog resource (a database or table) using Lake Formation's original, resource-by-resource grant model, the predecessor to the newer `aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions`, which additionally supports LF-Tag-based grants at scale.
aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions: `aws_lake_formation_principal_permissions` grants a real Lake Formation permission to a principal on a Data Catalog resource, AWS's current, recommended permission model, which supports both direct resource grants and LF-Tag-based access control for managing permissions across large numbers of databases and tables at once.
aws_lake_formation_resource: `aws_lake_formation_resource` registers a real S3 location with Lake Formation, the real prerequisite step that brings that storage location under Lake Formation's own permission model rather than leaving access to bucket policies and IAM alone.
aws_lake_formation_tag: `aws_lake_formation_tag` defines a real LF-Tag, a key with one or more allowed values, such as `department` with values `sales`, `marketing`, `engineering`, used as the building block of Lake Formation's tag-based access control.
aws_lake_formation_tag_association: `aws_lake_formation_tag_association` attaches a real `aws_lake_formation_tag` to a Data Catalog resource or table column, so that principals granted matching tags, rather than an explicit per-resource grant, gain access to it.
aws_lambda_alias: `aws_lambda_alias` creates a real named, mutable pointer to a specific published version of an `aws_lambda_function`, so callers can be redirected to a new version, or gradually shifted to one with weighted traffic, without changing the ARN they invoke.
aws_lambda_capacity_provider: `aws_lambda_capacity_provider` provisions a real pool of EC2 instances, with a chosen instance type, networking, and scaling configuration, that Lambda functions run on under Lambda Managed Instances, combining EC2-level compute control with Lambda's own serverless programming model. This is a genuinely new capability, so behavior here is verified live rather than assumed from general knowledge.
aws_lambda_code_signing_config: `aws_lambda_code_signing_config` defines a real policy that requires deployed Lambda function code to be signed by a trusted AWS Signer profile before Lambda will accept it, rejecting unsigned or tampered deployment packages.
aws_lambda_event_invoke_config: `aws_lambda_event_invoke_config` configures a real `aws_lambda_function`'s asynchronous-invocation behavior, retry attempts, maximum event age, and success/failure destinations, for invocations that don't wait synchronously for a response.
aws_lambda_event_source_mapping: `aws_lambda_event_source_mapping` creates a real subscription that polls a stream or queue, a Kinesis stream, a DynamoDB stream, an SQS queue, an MSK or self-managed Kafka topic, and invokes an `aws_lambda_function` with the batched records it reads.
aws_lambda_function: `aws_lambda_function` creates a real Lambda function: its deployment package or container image, runtime, handler, memory, timeout, and execution role, the real unit of code AWS Lambda runs on demand.
aws_lambda_layer_version: `aws_lambda_layer_version` publishes a real immutable version of a Lambda layer, a zip archive of libraries or other dependencies that one or more `aws_lambda_function`s can include without bundling that content into each function's own deployment package.
aws_lambda_layer_version_permission: `aws_lambda_layer_version_permission` grants a real other AWS account, or the whole account's organization, permission to use a specific `aws_lambda_layer_version`, letting a layer be shared without making it public.
aws_lambda_microvm_image: `aws_lambda_microvm_image` builds a real versioned image, a Dockerfile plus application artifacts uploaded to S3, that Lambda MicroVMs launch on demand as individually isolated, VM-level-sandboxed compute instances. This is a genuinely new AWS service: Lambda MicroVMs launched June 22, 2026, expanded from an initial five AWS Regions to ten as of August 2026, and is recent enough that not all of its behavior is covered by pre-2026 general knowledge.
aws_lambda_network_connector: `aws_lambda_network_connector` configures the real VPC networking, subnets and security groups, that an `aws_lambda_capacity_provider`'s underlying EC2 instances use to reach private resources under Lambda Managed Instances.
aws_lambda_permission: `aws_lambda_permission` grants a real resource-based permission on an `aws_lambda_function` or its alias, allowing a specific AWS service or account to invoke it, the mechanism behind, for example, API Gateway or S3 being allowed to call a function directly.
aws_lambda_resource_policy: `aws_lambda_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy directly to an `aws_lambda_function`, a lower-level, full-document alternative to granting individual permissions one at a time through `aws_lambda_permission`.
aws_lambda_url: `aws_lambda_url` creates a real, dedicated HTTPS endpoint for an `aws_lambda_function`, letting the function be invoked directly over HTTP without provisioning API Gateway in front of it.
aws_lambda_version: `aws_lambda_version` publishes a real, immutable numbered version of an `aws_lambda_function`'s current code and configuration, letting an `aws_lambda_alias` or a direct caller pin to a specific, unchanging version rather than the function's editable `$LATEST`.
aws_launch_configuration: `aws_launch_configuration` defines a real, legacy Auto Scaling launch template predecessor: instance type, AMI, and instance-level settings for instances an Auto Scaling group launches. AWS deprecated launch configurations in favor of `aws_launch_template`: no new EC2 features have been added to launch configurations since January 2023, and as of October 1, 2024 new AWS accounts cannot create a launch configuration through any method, console, API, CLI, or CloudFormation. Existing launch configurations in older accounts continue to function.
aws_launch_template: `aws_launch_template` defines a real, versioned template of instance launch parameters, AMI, instance type, key pair, security groups, and more, that EC2, Auto Scaling groups, EC2 Fleet, and Spot Fleet all launch instances from. It is the current, actively developed successor to the deprecated `aws_launch_configuration`, adding version history and support for the latest EC2 features.
aws_launch_wizard_deployment: `aws_launch_wizard_deployment` deploys a real, sized and configured workload, third-party software such as SQL Server or SAP, or a supported AWS workload pattern, using AWS Launch Wizard's own guided, Well-Architected-aligned automation rather than a hand-built template.
aws_lex_bot: `aws_lex_bot` creates a real Amazon Lex V2 conversational bot: its locales, intents, and IAM role. Lex V2 is the only Lex generation CloudFormation supports; the original Lex V1 has no CloudFormation resource type of its own.
aws_lex_bot_alias: `aws_lex_bot_alias` creates a real named pointer to a specific `aws_lex_bot_version`, letting a calling application be redirected to a new bot version, for example promoting a tested version to a `PROD` alias, without changing the identifier the application calls.
aws_lex_bot_version: `aws_lex_bot_version` publishes a real, immutable numbered snapshot of an `aws_lex_bot`'s current DRAFT configuration. If the DRAFT is unchanged since the last version was created, Amazon Lex returns that existing version rather than creating a duplicate.
aws_lex_resource_policy: `aws_lex_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_lex_bot` or its alias, controlling which principals, including from other accounts, can use it in a conversation.
aws_license_manager_grant: `aws_license_manager_grant` shares a real `aws_license_manager_license`'s entitlements with a specific AWS account, organizational unit, or organization, the mechanism a license owner uses to let another account consume a license it granted from AWS Marketplace or a direct seller integration.
aws_license_manager_license: `aws_license_manager_license` represents a real granted license for a product purchased from AWS Marketplace or from a seller integrated with AWS License Manager's managed entitlements, tracking the license's entitlements, validity period, and consumption rules.
aws_license_manager_license_asset_rule_s: `aws_license_manager_license_asset_rule_set` defines a real named set of rules that govern how an `aws_license_manager_license`'s usage is tracked and enforced against the physical or virtual assets consuming it. This resource type has only thin official documentation, an API reference entry rather than a full guide, verified live this session rather than assumed from general knowledge.
aws_lightsail_alarm: `aws_lightsail_alarm` creates a real CloudWatch-backed alarm scoped to a single Lightsail resource, an instance, database, distribution, or load balancer, notifying when one of that resource's own metrics crosses a threshold.
aws_lightsail_bucket: `aws_lightsail_bucket` creates a real Lightsail object storage bucket, built on S3, for storing files at Lightsail's simplified, predictable-pricing tier rather than through the full S3 console.
aws_lightsail_certificate: `aws_lightsail_certificate` provisions a real SSL/TLS certificate for use with Lightsail resources, such as a content delivery distribution, validated and issued the way an ACM certificate is but managed within Lightsail's own simplified surface.
aws_lightsail_container: `aws_lightsail_container` creates a real Lightsail Container Service, a managed environment that deploys and runs containerized applications, images pushed via Docker, without the operational surface of a full ECS or EKS cluster.
aws_lightsail_database: `aws_lightsail_database` creates a real managed relational database, MySQL or PostgreSQL, at Lightsail's simplified, flat-rate pricing tier, optionally with a High Availability option that runs a standby copy in a second Availability Zone.
aws_lightsail_database_snapshot: `aws_lightsail_database_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_lightsail_database`, which can later be restored into a new database instance.
aws_lightsail_disk: `aws_lightsail_disk` creates a real, SSD-based block storage volume that can be attached to a Lightsail instance for additional or persistent storage beyond the instance's own bundled disk.
aws_lightsail_disk_snapshot: `aws_lightsail_disk_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_lightsail_disk`, which can later be used to create a new disk with the same data.
aws_lightsail_distribution: `aws_lightsail_distribution` creates a real content delivery network distribution, powered by CloudFront under the hood, that caches and accelerates delivery of content hosted on a Lightsail instance, bucket, or load balancer.
aws_lightsail_domain: `aws_lightsail_domain` creates a real DNS zone within Lightsail for a registered domain, letting its DNS records be managed alongside other Lightsail resources rather than in Route 53 directly.
aws_lightsail_instance: `aws_lightsail_instance` creates a real virtual private server, a bundled combination of compute, storage, and a fixed data transfer allowance, at Lightsail's simplified, predictable monthly pricing.
aws_lightsail_instance_snapshot: `aws_lightsail_instance_snapshot` creates a real point-in-time snapshot of an `aws_lightsail_instance`, including its attached disks, which can later be used to launch a new instance with the same state.
aws_lightsail_load_balancer: `aws_lightsail_load_balancer` creates a real load balancer that distributes incoming traffic across multiple Lightsail instances, Lightsail's own simplified counterpart to an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer.
aws_lightsail_load_balancer_tls_certific: `aws_lightsail_load_balancer_tls_certificate` provisions a real TLS certificate attached to an `aws_lightsail_load_balancer`, so traffic reaching the load balancer over HTTPS terminates against a validated certificate.
aws_lightsail_static_ip: `aws_lightsail_static_ip` allocates a real static public IP address that can be attached to a Lightsail instance, keeping the instance reachable at a fixed address across stops, starts, and replacements.
aws_location_apikey: `aws_location_apikey` creates a real API key for authenticating requests to Amazon Location Service resources, maps, places, routes, trackers, an alternative to IAM credentials introduced for Location Service in January 2024 for simpler client-side and mobile use.
aws_location_geofence_collection: `aws_location_geofence_collection` creates a real collection of virtual geographic boundaries that Amazon Location Service monitors devices against, raising an event when a tracked device enters or leaves one.
aws_location_map: `aws_location_map` creates a real map resource in Amazon Location Service, backed by a chosen map style and data provider, for rendering interactive or static map imagery in an application.
aws_location_place_index: `aws_location_place_index` creates a real place index resource in Amazon Location Service, used to search for and geocode addresses, points of interest, and other place data against a chosen data provider.
aws_location_route_calculator: `aws_location_route_calculator` creates a real route calculator resource in Amazon Location Service, used to estimate travel time and distance and to generate turn-by-turn directions between locations.
aws_location_tracker: `aws_location_tracker` creates a real tracker resource in Amazon Location Service that ingests and stores the near-real-time location of devices, so their movement can be visualized on a map and evaluated against geofences.
aws_location_tracker_consumer: `aws_location_tracker_consumer` links a real `aws_location_tracker` to an `aws_location_geofence_collection` as its consumer, the association that lets a tracker's incoming location updates be evaluated against that collection's geofences.
aws_logs_account_policy: `aws_logs_account_policy` defines a real, account-wide CloudWatch Logs policy, a subscription filter or data protection policy applied by default, rather than configuring the same policy on every individual `aws_logs_log_group`.
aws_logs_delivery: `aws_logs_delivery` creates a real, active connection between an `aws_logs_delivery_source` and an `aws_logs_delivery_destination`, the resource that actually turns a configured source and destination into a flowing pipeline of vended logs.
aws_logs_delivery_destination: `aws_logs_delivery_destination` represents a real AWS service, CloudWatch Logs, S3, Firehose, or X-Ray, configured to receive vended logs through the newer CloudWatch Logs delivery framework, the target end of an `aws_logs_delivery`.
aws_logs_delivery_source: `aws_logs_delivery_source` represents a real AWS resource, such as a VPC or a Route 53 resolver, registered as a source of vended logs through the newer CloudWatch Logs delivery framework, the origin end of an `aws_logs_delivery`.
aws_logs_destination: `aws_logs_destination` creates a real cross-account subscription destination, most commonly a Kinesis stream, that another account's log group subscription filter can stream matching log events to. This is the older CloudWatch Logs subscription mechanism, distinct from the newer delivery-source/delivery-destination framework used by `aws_logs_delivery`.
aws_logs_integration: `aws_logs_integration` creates a real, zero-ETL integration between CloudWatch Logs and Amazon OpenSearch Service, currently the only supported integration type, enabling curated vended-log dashboards powered by OpenSearch analytics without a separate ingestion pipeline. Only one integration is currently supported per account, and an existing integration cannot be modified in place.
aws_logs_log_anomaly_detector: `aws_logs_log_anomaly_detector` creates a real machine-learning detector that regularly scans one or more log groups, learns the recurring text patterns in their log fields, and flags anomalies that break from those learned patterns.
aws_logs_log_group: `aws_logs_log_group` creates a real CloudWatch Logs log group, the container that log streams are organized under and that retention, encryption, and access settings are configured against.
aws_logs_log_stream: `aws_logs_log_stream` creates a real, individual sequence of log events within an `aws_logs_log_group`, typically one per source, an EC2 instance, a Lambda invocation, that log events actually get appended to.
aws_logs_metric_filter: `aws_logs_metric_filter` defines a real pattern that CloudWatch Logs evaluates against incoming events in an `aws_logs_log_group`, publishing a CloudWatch metric data point each time a log event matches, the mechanism behind turning free-text logs into alarmable numeric metrics.
aws_logs_query_definition: `aws_logs_query_definition` saves a real, named CloudWatch Logs Insights query for reuse from the console or API, rather than re-typing it for every ad hoc investigation.
aws_logs_resource_policy: `aws_logs_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy scoped to specific `aws_logs_log_group`s, controlling which other AWS services or accounts can write log events into them.
aws_logs_scheduled_query: `aws_logs_scheduled_query` runs a real `aws_logs_query_definition`-style Logs Insights query on a recurring schedule and delivers its results automatically to a configured destination, such as an S3 bucket or an EventBridge event bus.
aws_logs_storage_tier_policy: `aws_logs_storage_tier_policy` configures whether an `aws_logs_log_group`'s older log events automatically move to CloudWatch Logs' lower-cost Infrequent Access storage tier after a chosen age, trading slightly slower query performance for reduced storage cost.
aws_logs_subscription_filter: `aws_logs_subscription_filter` streams real log events matching a pattern from an `aws_logs_log_group` to a destination, a Kinesis stream, Firehose, or Lambda function, in near real time as they're ingested.
aws_logs_transformer: `aws_logs_transformer` attaches a real ordered pipeline of processors to an `aws_logs_log_group`, applying transformations to each log event at ingestion time so that later Logs Insights queries and metric filters can operate on the transformed, structured version rather than the raw text.
aws_lookout_equipment_inference_schedule: `aws_lookout_equipment_inference_scheduler` schedules real, recurring inference runs against a trained Amazon Lookout for Equipment model, feeding it fresh sensor data on a cadence and surfacing predicted anomalies. Lookout for Equipment closed to new customers on October 7, 2025, and AWS has stated it will be fully discontinued on October 7, 2026, a date roughly six weeks from now; existing customers can keep using it as normal until then, with AWS continuing security, availability, and performance investment but no new features.
aws_lookout_vision_project: `aws_lookout_vision_project` was a real project container for training and hosting Amazon Lookout for Vision computer-vision defect-detection models. Lookout for Vision is now fully discontinued: it closed to new customers on October 10, 2024, and shut down entirely on October 31, 2025, a date now in the past, so this resource describes a service no longer operable rather than a current one.
aws_m2_application: `aws_m2_application` defines a real mainframe application, its runtime engine (Micro Focus or Blue Age) and application definition, deployed onto an `aws_m2_environment` under AWS Mainframe Modernization. The Mainframe Modernization managed-runtime-environment experience closed to new customers on November 7, 2025; existing customers can continue using it as normal.
aws_m2_deployment: `aws_m2_deployment` deploys a real, specific `aws_m2_application` version onto an `aws_m2_environment`, the resource that actually promotes application code from registered to running under AWS Mainframe Modernization.
aws_m2_environment: `aws_m2_environment` creates a real managed runtime environment, the compute cluster that AWS Mainframe Modernization continually monitors and self-heals, that one or more `aws_m2_application`s run on. Like `aws_m2_application`, this closed to new customers on November 7, 2025; existing customers can continue using it as normal.
aws_macie_allow_list: `aws_macie_allow_list` defines a real list of text patterns or exact values, stored as an S3 object, that Amazon Macie should ignore when scanning for sensitive data, keeping known-benign content out of Macie's findings.
aws_macie_custom_data_identifier: `aws_macie_custom_data_identifier` defines a real, custom sensitive-data pattern, a regular expression with optional keyword and proximity rules, that Macie checks for during a scan beyond its own built-in managed data identifiers.
aws_macie_findings_filter: `aws_macie_findings_filter` defines real custom criteria, severity, finding type, affected resource, that either narrows which Macie findings a query returns or automatically archives findings matching those criteria, so routine noise doesn't have to be triaged by hand.
aws_macie_session: `aws_macie_session` enables Macie for an account, the real, account-level resource that must exist before any `aws_macie_findings_filter` or `aws_macie_custom_data_identifier` can be created.
aws_managed_blockchain_accessor: `aws_managed_blockchain_accessor` creates a real token-based access credential for Amazon Managed Blockchain's Ethereum node JSON-RPC APIs, an alternative to signing every request with SigV4 that instead authenticates with a bearer token.
aws_managed_blockchain_member: `aws_managed_blockchain_member` creates a real member identity within a Hyperledger Fabric network on Amazon Managed Blockchain, the account-level participant that peer nodes, `aws_managed_blockchain_node`, are created under.
aws_managed_blockchain_node: `aws_managed_blockchain_node` creates a real peer node running within an `aws_managed_blockchain_member`'s participation in a Hyperledger Fabric network on Amazon Managed Blockchain, the compute that actually executes chaincode and maintains the ledger.
aws_media_connect_bridge: `aws_media_connect_bridge` creates a real connection point between an on-premises data center and AWS, moving live video content from the cloud to a local facility or from a local facility to the cloud, depending on the chosen bridge type.
aws_media_connect_bridge_output: `aws_media_connect_bridge_output` defines a real destination that an `aws_media_connect_bridge` sends its content to, the bridge's own counterpart to a flow's `aws_media_connect_flow_output`.
aws_media_connect_bridge_source: `aws_media_connect_bridge_source` adds a real content source to an `aws_media_connect_bridge`, the specific inbound feed the bridge accepts and relays.
aws_media_connect_flow: `aws_media_connect_flow` creates a real managed transport between a live video source and one or more outputs, MediaConnect's original, source-to-outputs architecture for ingesting, distributing, and routing live video within and beyond AWS.
aws_media_connect_flow_entitlement: `aws_media_connect_flow_entitlement` grants a real other AWS account permission to create their own flow subscribed to this `aws_media_connect_flow`'s output, the mechanism MediaConnect uses to share a live feed across account boundaries.
aws_media_connect_flow_output: `aws_media_connect_flow_output` defines a real destination address, protocol, and port that an `aws_media_connect_flow` sends its ingested video to; a single flow can have up to 50 outputs.
aws_media_connect_flow_source: `aws_media_connect_flow_source` defines the real inbound video feed, its protocol and originating address, that an `aws_media_connect_flow` ingests from.
aws_media_connect_flow_vpc_interface: `aws_media_connect_flow_vpc_interface` attaches a real elastic network interface inside a VPC to an `aws_media_connect_flow`, letting the flow send or receive video privately within that VPC instead of over the public internet.
aws_media_connect_gateway: `aws_media_connect_gateway` creates a real on-premises software gateway that connects local infrastructure to AWS Elemental MediaConnect, the component an `aws_media_connect_bridge` uses to actually reach a data center.
aws_media_connect_router_input: `aws_media_connect_router_input` creates a real inbound connection point on the MediaConnect Router, a newer, cloud-native routing backbone that lets any registered feed be instantly connected to any registered destination across regions, distinct from MediaConnect's original per-flow architecture.
aws_media_connect_router_network_interfa: `aws_media_connect_router_network_interface` provisions a real public or VPC-scoped network interface that an `aws_media_connect_router_input` or router output uses to actually send or receive traffic, the underlying network plumbing beneath the MediaConnect Router's logical inputs and outputs.
aws_media_connect_router_output: `aws_media_connect_router_output` creates a real outbound destination on the MediaConnect Router that can receive media routed from one or more `aws_media_connect_router_input`s.
aws_media_convert_job_template: `aws_media_convert_job_template` saves a real, reusable set of MediaConvert transcoding job settings, output format, codec, bitrate, and destination queue, so new jobs can be created from the template instead of re-specifying every setting.
aws_media_convert_preset: `aws_media_convert_preset` saves real, reusable encoding settings for a single output within an `aws_media_convert_job_template` or job, letting the same output configuration, resolution, codec, bitrate, be applied across multiple jobs and overridden per job when needed.
aws_media_convert_queue: `aws_media_convert_queue` creates a real queue that MediaConvert transcoding jobs are submitted to and processed from, in ACTIVE or PAUSED state, with jobs of equal priority processed in the order they were submitted.
aws_media_live_channel: `aws_media_live_channel` creates a real live video encoding channel, MediaLive's core resource, that takes one or more `aws_media_live_input`s and encodes them into one or more outputs.
aws_media_live_channel_placement_group: `aws_media_live_channel_placement_group` organizes a real group of `aws_media_live_channel`s within an `aws_media_live_cluster`, so channels running on the same on-premises or Outposts infrastructure can be managed and allocated together.
aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_templat: `aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template` defines a real reusable CloudWatch alarm configuration for MediaLive resources, which can be applied consistently across channels rather than hand-configured per channel.

`aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template_group` groups real `aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template`s together so the group, rather than each template individually, can be attached to a MediaLive signal map or channel in one step.
aws_media_live_cluster: `aws_media_live_cluster` creates a real MediaLive Anywhere cluster, the on-premises or Outposts infrastructure grouping that `aws_media_live_channel_placement_group`s and their channels run on, letting MediaLive manage encoding workloads outside AWS's own data centers.
aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_templat: `aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template` defines a real reusable EventBridge rule for a MediaLive event type, a channel alert, an input change, a signal map alarm, and more, which can be applied consistently across resources rather than hand-configured per resource.
`aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template_group` groups real `aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template`s together so the group can be attached to a MediaLive signal map or channel in one step.
aws_media_live_input: `aws_media_live_input` defines a real video source, its type and connection details, that an `aws_media_live_channel` encodes from.
aws_media_live_input_security_group: `aws_media_live_input_security_group` defines a real set of allowed CIDR ranges that an `aws_media_live_input` accepts push-based input from, MediaLive's equivalent of a security group scoped to incoming video traffic.
aws_media_live_multiplex: `aws_media_live_multiplex` creates a real MPEG-TS multiplex, a single transport stream that carries multiple encoded programs bundled together for broadcast delivery, distinct from an `aws_media_live_channel`'s single-program encoding role.
aws_media_live_multiplexprogram: `aws_media_live_multiplexprogram` adds a real encoded program, video, audio, and metadata settings, into an `aws_media_live_multiplex`'s combined transport stream.
aws_media_live_network: `aws_media_live_network` defines a real network configuration, IP pools and routes, that MediaLive Anywhere uses so channels running on an `aws_media_live_cluster` can reach on-premises or Outposts network resources.
aws_media_live_node: `aws_media_live_node` registers a real physical or virtual compute unit into an `aws_media_live_cluster`, the actual hardware or instance that MediaLive Anywhere schedules channel encoding work onto.
aws_media_live_sdi_source: `aws_media_live_sdi_source` defines a real SDI (Serial Digital Interface) video input, hardware-connected rather than network-streamed, for MediaLive Anywhere to encode from an on-premises `aws_media_live_cluster`.
aws_media_live_signal_map: `aws_media_live_signal_map` discovers and visualizes a real media supply chain, MediaLive channels, MediaConnect flows, and related resources, starting from a chosen entry point ARN, and can attach `aws_media_live_cloud_watch_alarm_template`s and `aws_media_live_event_bridge_rule_template`s across everything it discovers.
aws_media_package_asset: `aws_media_package_asset` ingests a real video-on-demand asset through an `aws_media_package_channel`, the original MediaPackage architecture's VOD counterpart to its live-streaming role.
aws_media_package_channel: `aws_media_package_channel` creates a real entry point that receives a live video stream from an encoder such as MediaLive and prepares it for packaging, the original MediaPackage (v1) channel resource, now superseded for new deployments by `aws_media_package_v2_channel`.
aws_media_package_origin_endpoint: `aws_media_package_origin_endpoint` defines a real packaging configuration, HLS, DASH, CMAF, and more, on an `aws_media_package_channel`, the endpoint players actually request the packaged stream from.
aws_media_package_packaging_configuratio: `aws_media_package_packaging_configuration` defines a real output packaging format, HLS, DASH, CMAF, MSS, for on-demand assets within an `aws_media_package_packaging_group`.
aws_media_package_packaging_group: `aws_media_package_packaging_group` creates a real top-level container for `aws_media_package_packaging_configuration`s, the v1 MediaPackage VOD counterpart to a live channel.
aws_media_package_v2_channel: `aws_media_package_v2_channel` creates a real entry point that receives a live video stream from an encoder such as MediaLive, MediaPackage v2's redesigned channel resource, which supports low-latency HLS and ingesting via the CMAF-ingest protocol in addition to HLS, distinct from the original `aws_media_package_channel`.
aws_media_package_v2_channel_group: `aws_media_package_v2_channel_group` creates a real top-level MediaPackage v2 resource that one or more `aws_media_package_v2_channel`s belong to, providing a single, fixed egress domain shared across every channel in the group regardless of individual channel failures or upgrades.
aws_media_package_v2_channel_policy: `aws_media_package_v2_channel_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_media_package_v2_channel`, controlling which principals can ingest into or manage that channel.
aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint: `aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint` defines a real packaging configuration on an `aws_media_package_v2_channel`, the endpoint players actually request the packaged output stream from.
aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint_pol: `aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_media_package_v2_origin_endpoint`, controlling which principals can retrieve the packaged output from that endpoint.
aws_media_store_container: `aws_media_store_container` was a real storage container for live video origination in AWS Elemental MediaStore. MediaStore is now fully discontinued: AWS ended access to the MediaStore console and MediaStore resources on November 13, 2025, a date now in the past, recommending migration to S3 for simple live-streaming workflows or to MediaPackage for advanced ones. This resource describes a service no longer operable rather than a current one.
aws_media_tailor_channel: `aws_media_tailor_channel` creates a real linear, assembled streaming channel under MediaTailor's channel assembly workflow, stitching together video-on-demand and live sources with personalized ad insertion into one continuous stream.
aws_media_tailor_channel_policy: `aws_media_tailor_channel_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to an `aws_media_tailor_channel`, controlling which principals can retrieve its assembled output.
aws_media_tailor_function: `aws_media_tailor_function` defines a real custom function, an HTTP-backed endpoint with configurable headers, that MediaTailor can invoke as part of a sequential executor chain to run custom logic during ad decisioning or playback configuration. This resource has only thin official documentation, verified live this session against AWS's own CloudFormation reference and field schema rather than assumed from general knowledge, since it did not turn up a dedicated conceptual guide page the way MediaTailor's older resources do.
