aws_vpc_lattice_resource_policy: `aws_vpc_lattice_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based policy to an `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network`, controlling which principals or accounts can associate their own VPCs or services with it.
aws_vpc_lattice_rule: `aws_vpc_lattice_rule` defines a real routing rule on an `aws_vpc_lattice_listener`, matching request path or header conditions and directing matching traffic to a specific `aws_vpc_lattice_target_group`.
aws_vpc_lattice_service: `aws_vpc_lattice_service` creates a real, logical application service in VPC Lattice, with its own DNS name and `aws_vpc_lattice_listener`s, that consumers reach through an `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network` without VPC peering or Transit Gateway routes.
aws_vpc_lattice_service_network: `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network` creates a real, logical boundary that `aws_vpc_lattice_service`s are published into and VPCs are associated with, the resource that actually lets services and consuming VPCs across separate accounts and VPCs discover and reach each other.
aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_resource: `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_resource_association` associates a real `aws_vpc_lattice_resource_configuration` with an `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network`, making that non-service resource reachable to everything else connected to the network.
aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_service_: `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_service_association` associates a real `aws_vpc_lattice_service` with an `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network`, the resource that actually publishes the service so consumers on the network can reach it.
aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_vpc_asso: `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network_vpc_association` associates a real VPC with an `aws_vpc_lattice_service_network`, the resource that actually lets resources inside that VPC reach every service published to the network.
aws_vpc_lattice_target_group: `aws_vpc_lattice_target_group` defines a real set of targets, EC2 instances, IP addresses, Lambda functions, or an ALB, and their health check, that an `aws_vpc_lattice_rule` forwards matching traffic to.
aws_waf_byte_match_set: `aws_waf_byte_match_set` defines a real condition, matching a specific byte sequence in a request part, header, URI, body, that an `aws_waf_rule` references. This is part of AWS WAF Classic (global, for CloudFront), which AWS deprecated: support ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past. AWS's current, actively developed offering is AWS WAFv2 (`aws_wafv2_web_acl` and related resources).
aws_waf_ipset: `aws_waf_ipset` defines a real set of IP addresses or CIDR ranges that an `aws_waf_rule` references as a match condition. Like the rest of AWS WAF Classic, support for this resource ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past; AWS's current offering is AWS WAFv2.
aws_waf_rule: `aws_waf_rule` combines real match conditions, byte, IP set, size constraint, SQL injection, XSS, into a single rule that an `aws_waf_web_acl` evaluates against incoming requests, under AWS WAF Classic (global, for CloudFront). AWS WAF Classic support ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past; AWS's current, actively developed offering is AWS WAFv2.
aws_waf_size_constraint_set: `aws_waf_size_constraint_set` defines a real condition, matching a request part's size against a threshold, that an `aws_waf_rule` references. Like the rest of AWS WAF Classic, support for this resource ended September 30, 2025.
aws_waf_sql_injection_match_set: `aws_waf_sql_injection_match_set` defines a real condition, matching SQL-injection-like patterns in a request part, that an `aws_waf_rule` references. Like the rest of AWS WAF Classic, support for this resource ended September 30, 2025.
aws_waf_web_acl: `aws_waf_web_acl` creates a real, top-level web ACL under AWS WAF Classic (global, for CloudFront), evaluating its ordered list of `aws_waf_rule`s against every request and allowing or blocking based on the first match. AWS WAF Classic support ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past; AWS's current, actively developed offering is `aws_wafv2_web_acl`.
aws_waf_xss_match_set: `aws_waf_xss_match_set` defines a real condition, matching cross-site-scripting-like patterns in a request part, that an `aws_waf_rule` references. Like the rest of AWS WAF Classic, support for this resource ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_byte_match_set: `aws_wafregional_byte_match_set` defines a real condition, matching a specific byte sequence in a request part, that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references, the Regional (ALB/API Gateway) counterpart to `aws_waf_byte_match_set`'s global (CloudFront) scope. This is part of AWS WAF Classic, which AWS deprecated: support ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past. AWS's current, actively developed offering is AWS WAFv2.
aws_wafregional_geo_match_set: `aws_wafregional_geo_match_set` defines a real condition, matching a request's country of origin, that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references. Like the rest of AWS WAF Classic Regional, support for this resource ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_ipset: `aws_wafregional_ipset` defines a real set of IP addresses or CIDR ranges that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references, the Regional counterpart to `aws_waf_ipset`. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule: `aws_wafregional_rate_based_rule` defines a real rule under AWS WAF Classic Regional that automatically tracks request rate per source IP and blocks addresses that exceed a configured threshold, distinct from `aws_wafregional_rule`'s own static, condition-based matching. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past; AWS's current offering, AWS WAFv2, has its own built-in rate-based rule statement type.
aws_wafregional_regex_pattern_set: `aws_wafregional_regex_pattern_set` defines a real set of regular expressions that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references as a match condition. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_rule: `aws_wafregional_rule` combines real match conditions into a single rule that an `aws_wafregional_web_acl` evaluates, the Regional (ALB/API Gateway) counterpart to `aws_waf_rule`'s global (CloudFront) scope, under AWS WAF Classic. Support ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past; AWS's current, actively developed offering is AWS WAFv2.
aws_wafregional_size_constraint_set: `aws_wafregional_size_constraint_set` defines a real condition, matching a request part's size against a threshold, that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_sql_injection_match_set: `aws_wafregional_sql_injection_match_set` defines a real condition, matching SQL-injection-like patterns, that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_web_acl: `aws_wafregional_web_acl` creates a real, top-level web ACL under AWS WAF Classic Regional, evaluating its `aws_wafregional_rule`s against requests to an associated ALB or API Gateway. Support ended September 30, 2025, roughly eleven months in the past; AWS's current, actively developed offering is `aws_wafv2_web_acl`.
aws_wafregional_web_aclassociation: `aws_wafregional_web_aclassociation` attaches a real `aws_wafregional_web_acl` to a specific ALB or API Gateway stage, the resource that actually turns the ACL's rules on for that resource's traffic. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafregional_xss_match_set: `aws_wafregional_xss_match_set` defines a real condition, matching cross-site-scripting-like patterns, that an `aws_wafregional_rule` references. Support for AWS WAF Classic ended September 30, 2025.
aws_wafv2_ipset: `aws_wafv2_ipset` defines a real set of IP addresses or CIDR ranges that an `aws_wafv2_rule_group` or `aws_wafv2_web_acl` rule can match against, AWF WAFv2's current, actively developed counterpart to the deprecated `aws_waf_ipset`/`aws_wafregional_ipset`.
aws_wafv2_logging_configuration: `aws_wafv2_logging_configuration` streams a real log of every request an `aws_wafv2_web_acl` evaluates, along with which rule matched, to a CloudWatch Logs group, S3 bucket, or Firehose delivery stream.
aws_wafv2_regex_pattern_set: `aws_wafv2_regex_pattern_set` defines a real set of regular expressions that an `aws_wafv2_rule_group` or `aws_wafv2_web_acl` rule can match a request part against.
aws_wafv2_rule_group: `aws_wafv2_rule_group` defines a real, reusable, named set of WAFv2 rules that can be referenced from one or more `aws_wafv2_web_acl`s, so the same rule logic doesn't have to be redefined in every ACL that needs it.
aws_wafv2_web_acl: `aws_wafv2_web_acl` creates a real, top-level web ACL under AWS WAFv2, evaluating its own inline rules and any referenced `aws_wafv2_rule_group`s against requests to a CloudFront distribution, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync API, Cognito user pool, App Runner service, or Verified Access instance, one unified resource type across scopes that AWS WAF Classic split between global and Regional.
aws_wafv2_web_aclassociation: `aws_wafv2_web_aclassociation` attaches a real `aws_wafv2_web_acl` to a specific protected resource, an ALB, API Gateway stage, or similar, the resource that actually turns the ACL's rules on for that resource's traffic.
aws_well_architected_lens: `aws_well_architected_lens` defines a real, custom set of best-practice questions, beyond the standard Well-Architected Framework pillars, that can be applied to an `aws_well_architected_workload`'s review, for a specific industry or technology an organization wants to assess against.
aws_well_architected_profile: `aws_well_architected_profile` defines a real, reusable set of questions and priorities, tailored to a specific business context, that can be applied to an `aws_well_architected_workload`'s review, layered on top of the standard Well-Architected Framework pillars.
aws_well_architected_review_template: `aws_well_architected_review_template` defines a real, reusable review configuration, which lenses and pillars to include, that can be applied to an `aws_well_architected_workload`, so a consistent review structure can be reused across many workloads instead of configured individually each time.
aws_well_architected_workload: `aws_well_architected_workload` registers a real workload, an application or system, in the AWS Well-Architected Tool, the resource that a Well-Architected Framework review is actually conducted and tracked against.
aws_wickr_network: `aws_wickr_network` creates a real AWS Wickr network, the top-level, end-to-end-encrypted messaging environment that a Wickr organization's users, data retention bots, and admin API access are all scoped under. AWS Wickr launched admin APIs for programmatic network management in December 2025, roughly eight months ago.
aws_wisdom_aiagent: `aws_wisdom_aiagent` configures a real AI agent within an `aws_wisdom_assistant`, wiring together which `aws_wisdom_aiprompt`s and `aws_wisdom_aiguardrail`s it uses, under the generative-AI layer of Amazon Connect Wisdom (marketed as Amazon Q in Connect), for tasks like answer generation or self-service query handling.
aws_wisdom_aiagent_version: `aws_wisdom_aiagent_version` publishes a real, immutable version of an `aws_wisdom_aiagent`'s configuration, letting a specific, unchanging version be referenced rather than always using the agent's current, editable configuration.
aws_wisdom_aiguardrail: `aws_wisdom_aiguardrail` defines real content and behavior restrictions, denied topics, word filters, that an `aws_wisdom_aiagent` enforces on its generated responses, Amazon Q in Connect's own responsible-AI guardrail layer.
aws_wisdom_aiguardrail_version: `aws_wisdom_aiguardrail_version` publishes a real, immutable version of an `aws_wisdom_aiguardrail`'s configuration, letting a specific, unchanging version be referenced by an `aws_wisdom_aiagent`.
aws_wisdom_aiprompt: `aws_wisdom_aiprompt` defines a real, customized prompt template, for a specific purpose such as answer generation, case summarization, or email response, that an `aws_wisdom_aiagent` uses instead of Amazon Q in Connect's own built-in default prompt for that purpose.
aws_wisdom_aiprompt_version: `aws_wisdom_aiprompt_version` publishes a real, immutable version of an `aws_wisdom_aiprompt`'s text, letting a specific, unchanging version be referenced by an `aws_wisdom_aiagent`.
aws_wisdom_assistant: `aws_wisdom_assistant` creates a real Wisdom assistant, the top-level container that `aws_wisdom_knowledge_base`s, `aws_wisdom_aiagent`s, and `aws_wisdom_message_template`s are organized under, typically associated with an Amazon Connect instance to power agent assist or Amazon Q in Connect.
aws_wisdom_assistant_association: `aws_wisdom_assistant_association` links a real `aws_wisdom_assistant` to an external resource, most commonly an `aws_wisdom_knowledge_base`, that it should draw on, the resource that actually wires the two together.
aws_wisdom_knowledge_base: `aws_wisdom_knowledge_base` creates a real content source, synced from S3, a website, or a supported connector, that an `aws_wisdom_assistant`'s AI agents retrieve information from to ground their generated answers.
aws_wisdom_message_template: `aws_wisdom_message_template` defines a real, reusable response template, chat, email, or SMS, with variable placeholders, that a contact center agent or an `aws_wisdom_aiagent` can insert into a conversation instead of typing the same response by hand each time.
aws_wisdom_message_template_version: `aws_wisdom_message_template_version` publishes a real, immutable version of an `aws_wisdom_message_template`'s content, letting a reference to it pin to a specific, unchanging version rather than the template's editable draft.
aws_wisdom_quick_response: `aws_wisdom_quick_response` creates a real, short, reusable response, a canned answer to a common question, that an `aws_wisdom_assistant` surfaces to a contact center agent to insert into a conversation instead of typing it by hand each time.
aws_work_spaces_connection_alias: `aws_work_spaces_connection_alias` registers a real custom domain name that can be used to connect to an `aws_work_spaces_workspace` across accounts (in a multi-Region resilience or cross-account access setup), instead of connecting through WorkSpaces' own default registration code.
aws_work_spaces_thin_client_environment: `aws_work_spaces_thin_client_environment` creates a real, managed environment for WorkSpaces Thin Client devices, physical, purpose-built hardware for connecting to virtual desktops, controlling their software updates, maintenance windows, and device policies centrally rather than device by device.
aws_work_spaces_web_browser_settings: `aws_work_spaces_web_browser_settings` defines real, reusable browser policy settings, extensions, bookmarks, download behavior, that an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal` applies to every browsing session under Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser, a separate, browser-only product from classic `aws_work_spaces_workspace` full desktops.
aws_work_spaces_web_data_protection_sett: `aws_work_spaces_web_data_protection_settings` configures real inline data-loss-prevention rules, redacting or blocking sensitive data patterns in the browser, that an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal` enforces during a session.
aws_work_spaces_web_identity_provider: `aws_work_spaces_web_identity_provider` connects a real SAML or OIDC identity provider to an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal`, so end users authenticate with their existing corporate identity before a secure browsing session starts.
aws_work_spaces_web_ip_access_settings: `aws_work_spaces_web_ip_access_settings` defines a real, reusable allow-list of IP ranges that an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal` restricts session access to, keeping the portal reachable only from expected corporate networks.
aws_work_spaces_web_network_settings: `aws_work_spaces_web_network_settings` defines a real VPC, subnets, and security groups that an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal`'s browsing sessions actually run inside, so outbound traffic from the managed browser can reach private, VPC-only resources.
aws_work_spaces_web_portal: `aws_work_spaces_web_portal` creates a real Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser portal, a fully managed, isolated, in-browser session, that end users connect to instead of a full `aws_work_spaces_workspace` virtual desktop, when only web access, not a whole OS, is what's actually needed.
aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger: `aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger` configures real session logging, screen recording or event logs delivered to S3, for an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal`, for compliance or security review of what happened during a browsing session.
aws_work_spaces_web_trust_store: `aws_work_spaces_web_trust_store` imports real, trusted root certificates into an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal`, so its managed browser trusts internal, privately signed HTTPS endpoints that a public CA wouldn't otherwise validate.
aws_work_spaces_web_user_access_logging_: `aws_work_spaces_web_user_access_logging_settings` configures real logging of user access events, sign-ins and session starts, for an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal`, delivered to CloudWatch Logs.
aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings: `aws_work_spaces_web_user_settings` defines real, reusable end-user permissions, whether copy/paste, printing, or file transfer is allowed, that an `aws_work_spaces_web_portal` applies to every session.
aws_work_spaces_workspace: `aws_work_spaces_workspace` creates a real, persistent virtual desktop, Windows or Linux, that a user connects to with a WorkSpaces client, Amazon WorkSpaces' original, full-desktop product distinct from the browser-only `aws_work_spaces_web_portal`.
aws_work_spaces_workspace_ip_group: `aws_work_spaces_workspace_ip_group` defines a real, reusable allow-list of IP ranges that an `aws_work_spaces_workspace` restricts client connections to.
aws_workspaces_instances_volume: `aws_workspaces_instances_volume` creates a real EBS volume attached to an `aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_instance`, under WorkSpaces Core's newer, EC2-based managed-instance architecture, distinct from classic `aws_work_spaces_workspace`'s own bundled storage model.
aws_workspaces_instances_volume_associat: `aws_workspaces_instances_volume_association` attaches a real `aws_workspaces_instances_volume` to a specific `aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_instance`, the resource that actually represents the attach action rather than the volume itself.
aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_insta: `aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_instance` launches a real EC2 instance directly into the calling account as a managed WorkSpaces Core desktop, under WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances' newer architecture, which places compute in the customer's own account rather than an account owned by the WorkSpaces service the way classic `aws_work_spaces_workspace` does.
aws_workspaces_pool: `aws_workspaces_pool` creates a real pool of non-persistent, session-based virtual desktops that are provisioned on demand and torn down after use, WorkSpaces' pooled-desktop model for shared or task-worker use cases, distinct from a `aws_work_spaces_workspace`'s own persistent, one-user-per-desktop model.
aws_xray_group: `aws_xray_group` defines a real, named filter expression over X-Ray trace data, so traces matching specific criteria, an error rate threshold or a particular service, can be viewed and alarmed on as their own group rather than sifted out of the account's full trace volume by hand.
aws_xray_resource_policy: `aws_xray_resource_policy` attaches a real resource-based access policy to X-Ray, controlling which principals, including from other accounts, can send trace data into it.

data_aws_workspaces_account_modification: `aws_workspaces_account_modifications` reads the real, historical modifications made to WorkSpaces account settings.
data_aws_workspaces_application_associat: `aws_workspaces_application_associations` reads the real associations between a WorkSpaces application and a bundle or image.
data_aws_workspaces_applications: `aws_workspaces_applications` looks up a real WorkSpaces Application, an app deployable onto WorkSpaces Personal desktops via App Manager.
data_aws_workspaces_available_management: `aws_workspaces_available_management_cidr_ranges` reads the real, available CIDR ranges for WorkSpaces' own management network interface.
data_aws_workspaces_bundle_associations: `aws_workspaces_bundle_associations` reads the real applications associated with a WorkSpaces bundle.
data_aws_workspaces_client_branding: `aws_workspaces_client_branding` reads the real client branding (logo, support links) configured for a WorkSpaces directory.
data_aws_workspaces_client_properties: `aws_workspaces_client_properties` reads the real client device properties configured for a WorkSpaces directory.
data_aws_workspaces_connection_alias_per: `data_aws_workspaces_connection_alias_permissions` looks up a real, already-existing `aws_work_spaces_connection_alias`. It registers a real custom domain name that can be used to connect to an `aws_work_spaces_workspace` across accounts (in a multi-Region resilience or cross-account access setup), instead of connecting through WorkSpaces' own default registration code.
data_aws_workspaces_custom_workspace_ima: `aws_workspaces_custom_workspace_image_import` reads the real, current status of importing a custom WorkSpaces image.
data_aws_workspaces_image_associations: `aws_workspaces_image_associations` reads the real applications associated with a WorkSpaces image.
data_aws_workspaces_instances_instance_t: `aws_workspaces_instances_instance_types` reads the real, available EC2 instance types for a WorkSpaces Instances deployment.
data_aws_workspaces_instances_tags_for_r: `aws_workspaces_instances_tags_for_resource` reads the real tags applied to a WorkSpaces Instances resource.
data_aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_: `aws_workspaces_instances_workspace_instances` looks up a real WorkSpaces Instances EC2 instance, a self-managed desktop provisioned through WorkSpaces.
data_aws_workspaces_web_session: `aws_workspaces_web_session` looks up one real WorkSpaces Secure Browser session.
data_aws_workspaces_web_sessions: `aws_workspaces_web_sessions` reads the real WorkSpaces Secure Browser sessions on a portal.
data_aws_workspaces_web_tags_for_resourc: `aws_workspaces_web_tags_for_resource` reads the real tags applied to a WorkSpaces Secure Browser resource.
data_aws_workspaces_workspace_associatio: `aws_workspaces_workspace_associations` reads the real applications associated with a specific WorkSpace.
data_aws_workspaces_workspace_directorie: `aws_workspaces_workspace_directories` looks up a real WorkSpaces directory, the Active Directory or Identity Center registration WorkSpaces are provisioned against.
data_aws_workspaces_workspace_image_perm: `aws_workspaces_workspace_image_permissions` reads which real AWS accounts a WorkSpaces image has been shared with.
data_aws_workspaces_workspace_snapshots: `aws_workspaces_workspace_snapshots` reads the real, automatic snapshots taken of a WorkSpace.
data_aws_workspaces_workspaces_connectio: `aws_workspaces_workspaces_connection_status` reads the real, current connection status of a WorkSpace.
data_aws_workspaces_workspaces_pool_sess: `aws_workspaces_workspaces_pool_sessions` reads the real, active user sessions within a WorkSpaces Pools non-persistent pool.
data_aws_xray_encryption_config: `aws_xray_encryption_config` reads the real, account-wide encryption configuration for X-Ray trace data.
data_aws_xray_groups: `data_aws_xray_groups` looks up a real, already-existing `aws_xray_group`. It defines a real, named filter expression over X-Ray trace data, so traces matching specific criteria, an error rate threshold or a particular service, can be viewed and alarmed on as their own group rather than sifted out of the account's full trace volume by hand.
data_aws_xray_indexing_rules: `aws_xray_indexing_rules` reads the real indexing rules controlling which X-Ray trace attributes are searchable.
data_aws_xray_insight: `aws_xray_insight` looks up one real X-Ray Insight, an automatically detected anomaly in a traced service.
data_aws_xray_insight_impact_graph: `aws_xray_insight_impact_graph` reads the real service graph showing which downstream services an X-Ray Insight impacted.
data_aws_xray_insight_summaries: `aws_xray_insight_summaries` reads a real, summarized listing of X-Ray Insights.
data_aws_xray_resource_policies: `data_aws_xray_resource_policies` looks up a real, already-existing `aws_xray_resource_policy`. It attaches a real resource-based access policy to X-Ray, controlling which principals, including from other accounts, can send trace data into it.
data_aws_xray_retrieved_traces: `aws_xray_retrieved_traces` reads the real traces retrieved by an X-Ray Transaction Search retrieval job.
data_aws_xray_retrieved_traces_graph: `aws_xray_retrieved_traces_graph` reads the real service graph generated from an X-Ray Transaction Search retrieval job.
data_aws_xray_sampling_statistic_summari: `aws_xray_sampling_statistic_summaries` reads real, aggregated statistics on how X-Ray's own sampling rules are being applied.
data_aws_xray_sampling_targets: `aws_xray_sampling_targets` reads the real, computed sampling rates a service should apply for a given X-Ray sampling rule.
data_aws_xray_service_graph: `aws_xray_service_graph` reads the real service graph X-Ray generated from traced requests over a time window.
data_aws_xray_tags_for_resource: `aws_xray_tags_for_resource` reads the real tags applied to an X-Ray resource.
data_aws_xray_time_series_service_statis: `aws_xray_time_series_service_statistics` reads real, time-series statistics (latency, error rate) for a service in the X-Ray service graph.
data_aws_xray_trace_graph: `aws_xray_trace_graph` reads the real service graph for one specific X-Ray trace.
data_aws_xray_trace_segment_destination: `aws_xray_trace_segment_destination` reads the real, configured destination (X-Ray or CloudWatch Logs) traces are sent to.
data_aws_xray_trace_summaries: `aws_xray_trace_summaries` reads a real, summarized listing of X-Ray traces matching a filter expression.
